regions.summary: Commands >=$40 clear the initialization cursor after masking to six bits. Form an eight-byte song pointer record at $9A00+(command-1)*8; initialize one channel pointer per call, advancing the cursor by two until four pairs are loaded. Then enable channel mask $1D, clear loop counters and enable the four APU channels.

phase1.label: LegacyBank10TransitionPrefix

regions.summary: Historical main-transition prefix at CPU $81DC under physical banks [10,11,14,15]. regions.summary: Disable rendering and initialize display, stage pointers, graphics, player, palette, objects and OAM. For progression index below eight, stage records start at CPU $F000+stage*$100 and object grids at $8000+stage*$400 under their respective bank contexts. Install callback $80CE, reset stack and enter RAM $0770. The 32-byte source at RamTimingAndWaitTemplate supplies RAM $0760..$077F, including $0770. Progression >=8 hides sprites and jumps through the fixed mapper-4 scene entry; complete natural ending progression remains unproven.

phase1.evidence: Independent round004 review: analysis/round-004/review-notes.md; fresh-decode.json, fresh-reference-census.json and byte-checks.json. Physical end8116 is independently next accepted routine start. Preceding3byteJSR boundary agrees but itscallee and ordinary return are expressly not required/proposed. Exact closed self-directed control plus independently bounded fragment is stronger than legal decoding alone.

Successively halves that bound while alternating the mask, filling the 64-byte buffer at $0780. Lookup bytes and exact segment counts are preserved; no particular waveform name is asserted.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

units.summary: Subtract camera/progression offsets from depth, reject values outside two coarse bands and read paired 128-entry quantized tables. Multiply the lateral magnitude, reject excessive high/magnitude results and fold the accepted value around the center by side. Zero height succeeds immediately; nonzero height uses the shared multiply/shift arithmetic. Carry set rejects the coordinate, carry clear returns projected lateral/depth/height.

phase1.evidence: Direct JSR callee entry under source effective bank context; bounded callee-only closure, no assumption about post-call bank preservation. analysis/round-001/call-closure-evidence.json

Merges directional state in grouped pairs; differences against the latched state increment edge counters for masks $10/$20/$40/$80, with feedback tones on the first two. Writes a phase-derived strobe afterward. Counter meanings follow their consumers rather than a universal button-name assumption.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

units.name: UpdatePlayerMotionDispatch
units.summary: Clears coarse-position-change and forward-step bytes. Run mode selects an automatic step; pause/special flags can suppress updates. A transition path eases horizontal position toward $80 and elevation toward zero, then advances display/score counters. Other paths dispatch normal lateral and forward movement. The clamp and connected call continuations are now explicit under the reviewed bank contracts.

A transition path eases horizontal position toward $80 and elevation toward zero, then advances display/score counters. Other paths dispatch normal lateral and forward movement. The clamp and connected call continuations are now explicit under the reviewed bank contracts.

units.name: UpdateLateralMotion
units.summary: Uses raw and latched directional bits plus player flags to choose left/right movement. Updates the wrapped horizontal camera position by one or two and derives effect phase from its low six bits. In the special path also moves player horizontal position by three, clamping to $20..$DF. The shared decrement/increment entries preserve carry into the one-bit scroll high byte.

phase1.evidence: Round001 connected gameplay discovery; analysis/round-001/discovery-gameplay-1000.json; accepted trace roots and control-flow traversal under explicit mapper2 context; RAM upload origin not inferred.

units.name: UpdatePlayerElevation
units.summary: Normal motion settles elevation toward zero, checks six adjacent mask-buffer entries, and starts a jump-like state from the input edge counter. State 1 uses a two-unit rise/fall with a hold threshold; states 2 and later use mirrored lookup increments and a delayed apex. Landing clears state/elevation, sets an animation timer, and programs a pulse tone. Falling past $C0 takes a session/player reset path. Jump names are inferred from elevation and input behavior.

units.name: UpdateTimedMeter
units.summary: A signed initialization phase increases the meter every eight frame ticks up to $13 with tone feedback. Paused/run/special states gate updates; the precise game resource represented by the meter is unresolved.

The active phase counts down every $C0 eligible calls, updates a ten-byte display from lookup-selected text and blinks a sprite attribute. Expiry enters player flag $04 and requests sound $45. Paused/run/special states gate updates; the precise game resource represented by the meter is unresolved.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

The active phase counts down every $C0 eligible calls, updates a ten-byte display from lookup-selected text and blinks a sprite attribute. Expiry enters player flag $04 and requests sound $45. Paused/run/special states gate updates; the precise game resource represented by the meter is unresolved.

units.name: EmitMetaspriteRecord
units.summary: Consumes four-byte records: signed/wrapping Y delta, tile, attributes, and X delta. Deltas accumulate in the current sprite position; a leading $FF terminates successfully with carry clear. A zero next-sprite offset means no capacity; wrapping the offset after a write sets carry. Caller supplies a valid pointer and timing; no table extents beyond consumed records are inferred.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

Deltas accumulate in the current sprite position; a leading $FF terminates successfully with carry clear. A zero next-sprite offset means no capacity; wrapping the offset after a write sets carry. Caller supplies a valid pointer and timing; no table extents beyond consumed records are inferred.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

units.name: UpdatePrimaryMovingObject
units.summary: Tracks active state and palette phase, then moves a depth-like coordinate back and forth with stage-dependent steps and accumulating fractions. Other wrapped phases select folded lookup positions. Projection produces screen coordinates; bounded three-axis difference tests detect an auxiliary-effect hit or player contact, updating player/sound flags. Stores a four-byte history entry plus a render request and manages the primary cooldown/termination. The connected hit/reinitialize continuations and sixty sprite records are now explicit; multipart game identity remains unresolved.

units.name: UpdatePrimaryMovingObject
units.summary: Tracks active state and palette phase, then moves a depth-like coordinate back and forth with stage-dependent steps and accumulating fractions. Other wrapped phases select folded lookup positions. Projection produces screen coordinates; bounded three-axis difference tests detect an auxiliary-effect hit or player contact, updating player/sound flags. Stores a four-byte history entry plus a render request and manages the primary cooldown/termination. The connected hit/reinitialize continuations and sixty sprite records are now explicit; multipart game identity remains unresolved.

units.name: RenderMovingObjectRequest
units.summary: Consumes a four-byte render request and clears its active/depth byte. Rejects depth outside $40 or $60 according to display mode, then selects frame pointers from depth-to-frame lookup and request style. Primary direction, alternate display, effect phase and an eight-frame animation bit choose the pointer table. Tail-calls the common metasprite decoder.

phase1.evidence: Round001 validated reset/NMI contextual traversal and observed instruction roots; analysis/round-001/discovery-large*.json. Mapper2 effective 8KiB bank context retained; unresolved indirect dispatch excluded.

units.name: SubmitSoundChannelShadows
units.summary: Handles signed sound stop commands or delegates a positive sequence command. Otherwise shifts a channel mask and submits enabled pulse/triangle/noise shadow registers. Pulse 2 honors the immediate-effect duration before sequencer writes; note flags select silence, held volume, or new timer values. Two logical pulse-2 shadows are visited sequentially, so later enabled writes can supersede earlier ones.

units.name: AdvanceSoundChannelEnvelopes
units.summary: Iterates five logical channel states: 12 bytes per zero-page state and 16 bytes per register shadow. For enabled channels, decrements note duration; expiry decodes the next command. Otherwise advances a fractional envelope index, clamps it to 15, and reads a volume byte through the channel envelope pointer into its shadow.

regions.summary: Read channel stream bytes until emitting a note/rest or requesting stop. Below $C0 selects pitch and duration; $C0..$CF emits rests; $D0..$D7 performs a counted branch with a two-byte target; $D8..$DF selects pitch; $E0..$EF selects envelope. $F8 consumes a rate parameter, $F9..$FE selects duration backing and $FF requests global stop. Other high commands advance one byte. This mechanical grammar does not prove full natural command usage or complete song-table schema.

regions.summary: Dispatch vertical transition or active object-page updates. On coarse-position change, build a sixteen-byte RAM-record pointer in $05xx and a stage-grid pointer, rotate the page selector modulo four and fetch four type bytes. For each type, select mapper 0 to read its grid byte, restore mapper 6, parse it and advance the record cursor by $10. Stage<8 selects one of eight 1 KiB grids. Parser writes remain in the sixteen-byte RAM record; this does not establish all type meanings or natural selector use.

editorial_audit.notes: Final targeted editorial acceptance; ROM structurally incomplete: 13 unknown bytes in eight fragments. Reused 564 valid reviewed units; inspected inventory, locations, aliases, unknown notes and meaningful transfers to generated labels. Ten jump-target identifiers now describe mechanics. Removed stale complete-record reference from generic nine-byte scene gap. Normalized nested audit-unit records using existing physically containing reviewed units; no new semantic review credit or classification inferred. See editorial-audit.md.
findings: Ten generic jump targets renamed by mechanical role.
Stale SceneSpriteRecord010C87 reference removed from generic gap.
Nested audit-unit schema reconciled with existing physical extents.
Uncertain mechanics, reachability and progression remain explicit.
Inventory source locations made relative to commentary/source as required by audit.
Seven compressed or redundant unknown-boundary notes rewritten in plain prose; historical-call uncertainty retained. Wrapper stack-byte wording clarified.
Ninety-nine additional top-level data/image unit identities attached to physically overlapping records so audit checks every one of the 564 distinct units.

units.name: Bank2ReturnStub
units.summary: Returns immediately; no state is changed. This isolated entry has no further body.

units.name: Bank8DisableRenderingEntry
units.summary: Disable rendering and local control, then enter the bank8 scene initializer. The reviewed continuation runs the full sprite animation and local sound sequence. Safe return through its stack-page marker write depends on the explicit artificial SP=$F8 entry contract; natural ending completion is not established.

units.name: InitializeBank8SceneGraphics
units.summary: Copy sixteen scene seed bytes from CPU $8031 into zero page $50..$5F, then sixteen palette bytes into $80..$8F. Upload sixteen pages of scene patterns from CPU $A000 to PPU $0000 under banks 8/9 and reset control/scroll. The local seed layout supplies the initial scene coordinates and selectors.

units.name: Bank8InstallStackByteAndSetup
units.summary: Write marker $36 at RAM $0102, then tail-call the scene graphics initializer. With the reviewed entry SP=$F8 this does not overwrite live return slots. That concrete precondition does not establish safety for arbitrary stack positions or normal ending reachability.

units.name: Bank10PresentationEntry
units.summary: Jumps past the two unclassified bytes to the bank-local presentation setup.

units.name: RunBank10Presentation
units.summary: Uploads graphics, delays, and enables background rendering. Each wait updates a horizontal-scroll countdown and palette; a wrapping frame counter eventually times out. The controller result or timeout selects a byte from CPU $8003/$8004 into $F9. Rendering is disabled and the routine waits for the sampled buttons to be released before returning. The screen and selected byte meanings remain uncertain.

units.name: InitializeBank10Graphics
units.summary: Disables rendering, resets the PPU address latch, copies 16 pages from CPU $8800 to PPU $0000 and four pages from $9800 to $2000 (the shared pointer advances). Clears four pages at PPU $2C00, resets scrolling, and clears bit 3 of the byte mirrored to $4025. The expansion write effect is uncertain on this cartridge.

units.name: CopyBank10PagesAndPalette
units.summary: Copies X pages of 256 bytes from ($E0/$E1) to the PPU data port, advancing the source high byte. Then copies 16 bytes from CPU $81BC into zero page $80..$8F. Thus the palette seed copy also runs after each graphics upload.

units.name: DelayBank10NestedCounters
units.summary: Busy-waits with repeated zero-page reads. $45 is the inner wrapping countdown and $46 the outer countdown; entry values determine the delay, with zero representing a full wrap.

units.name: ReadBank10SelectedButtons
units.summary: Latches controller 1 and shifts four serial reads into $45. Comparing each masked read with one uses carry as the input bit. Returns the selected bits masked by $05; this is not a complete eight-button poll.

units.name: UploadBank10PaletteFromZeroPage
units.summary: Selects zero-page $80 as the indirect palette source and jumps to the shared 16-byte palette upload.

units.name: UploadBank10Palette16
units.summary: Uploads 16 source bytes through ($EE/$EF) to PPU palette $3F00. Resets the PPU address/scroll latches and disables PPU control before returning. Caller must have rendering timing under control; no vblank wait occurs here.

units.name: InitializeMainSession
units.summary: Enables interrupts, initializes display records, clears progression and alternate-display state, selects run mode 1, and initializes the timed display state. Calls use lower physical PRG banks 12/13 (mapper value 6); the fixed upper banks are 14/15.

units.name: InitializeMainScreen
units.summary: Disable rendering and initialize display, stage pointers, graphics, player, palette, objects and OAM. For progression index below eight, stage records start at CPU $F000+stage*$100 and object grids at $8000+stage*$400 under their respective bank contexts. Install callback $80CE, reset stack and enter RAM $0770. The 32-byte source at RamTimingAndWaitTemplate supplies RAM $0760..$077F, including $0770. Progression >=8 hides sprites and jumps through the fixed mapper-4 scene entry; complete natural ending progression remains unproven.

units.name: DelayMainScreenLoop
units.summary: Runs a 256-iteration Y countdown with repeated zero-page reads. X is untouched; timing rather than a computed result is the apparent purpose.

units.name: RunMainFrameCallback
units.summary: Visible frame work submits queued PPU text and palettes, starts sprite DMA from page $02, increments the 16-bit frame tick, and calls scrolling, input, player/object, display and sound updates. The callback continuation joins the reviewed update path; its return/stack behavior follows the fixed-bank NMI trampoline.

units.name: ApplyMainScrollAndMask
units.summary: Derives a small scroll perturbation from alternate-display state and the frame tick, subtracts it from the two-byte scroll position, and writes horizontal scroll plus nametable selection. Enables rendering with mask $1E and decrements the first sprite Y byte.

units.name: InitializePlayerWorkingState
units.summary: Clears zero page $10..$DF, then seeds rendering mask, horizontal position $80, elevation and motion/state counters. Clears the first auxiliary sprite-list byte. The initial clear deliberately leaves progression fields $E0 and above intact.

units.name: HideMainSprites
units.summary: Writes offscreen Y $F4 at every fourth byte in the sprite DMA page starting at offset 8. Reserves the first two sprites and resets the next sprite byte offset to 8.

units.name: DispatchMainStateTransitions
units.summary: Advance the first sprite Y byte, reset the stack and dispatch transition work from coarse-position change $DD, run mode and player flags. Reviewed palette/object/graphics calls preserve or restore mapper 6. Join the shared initialization or call RAM $0770 under the NMI dispatch convention; residual bytes immediately after that call remain unclassified.

units.name: MainTransitionPalettePrefix
units.summary: Copy the stage palette tail, clear auxiliary/effect state and seed stage palette fields into three render records. Initialize multipart objects and alternate graphics, then enable the running PPU mode. The fixed graphics wrapper restores mapper 6 before the continuation.

units.name: MainPaletteRefreshPrefix
units.summary: Refresh the stage palette and alternate palette segments, call the primary fixed-bank graphics loader and enable the running PPU mode. The reviewed graphics return restores mapper 6.

units.name: CopyStagePaletteTail
units.summary: Copies stage-record bytes $49..$4B through the indirect stage pointer to palette-shadow bytes $071D..$071F.

units.name: SilenceMainChannels
units.summary: Clears the pulse-1, pulse-2, triangle and noise control registers plus the sound-channel mask. Sets the pending sound command to $80 for the later sound update.

units.name: RenderWithAdjustedEffectPhase
units.summary: Temporarily subtracts the low five phase bits from the wrapped effect accumulator, calls the raster-effect routine, then restores those bits. The seven-bit accumulator wraps modulo 128.

units.name: RenderRasterEffect
units.summary: Prepares effect parameters and tests the sprite-zero-hit flag. May transfer to a RAM timing helper; otherwise visits 63 scanline entries, combining per-line masks, a phase mask and fractional carry into scroll writes. Finalizes scroll and PPU mask, then decrements RAM helper byte $0767. Rendering purpose is inferred from the timed PPU writes; the RAM helper implementation is not classified here.

units.name: AdvanceRasterEffectStep
units.summary: Avoids redundant PPU-mask writes, adds the fractional step to a six-bit accumulator, folds carry into the scroll accumulator, and cycles a three-step timing counter. NOPs and repeated paths are timing-sensitive and retained exactly.

units.name: InitializeRasterEffectState
units.summary: Builds fractional step, scroll accumulator and phase mask from the current effect bytes. Initializes the RAM helper activity byte and chooses PPU mask $0A or $1E from player/mode flags. Specific visual meaning of those state flags remains tentative.

units.name: InitializeRasterLineBuffers
units.summary: Builds the phase buffer, then fills 64 PPU-mask entries with $1E and 64 selector-mask entries with zero or $FF according to run mode.

units.name: BuildRasterPhaseBuffer
units.summary: Uses the high three bits of $23 to choose a mask and its low five bits as an initial segment bound. Successively halves that bound while alternating the mask, filling the 64-byte buffer at $0780. Lookup bytes and exact segment counts are preserved; no particular waveform name is asserted.

units.name: UploadMainPalette32
units.summary: Selects one of three 32-byte palette shadows at $0700/$0720/$0740 from display state, uploads to PPU $3F00, and resets the PPU address latch. Calls require appropriate rendering timing; this routine itself does not wait for vblank.

units.name: InitializeMainPaletteAndRaster
units.summary: Initializes palette and RAM timing bytes, uploads the palette, then initializes raster line buffers.

units.name: CopyStagePaletteVariantA
units.summary: Copy stage-record fields $42/$43 and $45..$47 into selected palette-shadow slots. Stage records use CPU $F000+stage*$100 for stage<8; these known fields do not establish the meaning of every byte in each page.

units.name: CopyStagePaletteVariantB
units.summary: Copies the alternate stage-record fields $2A/$2B and $39..$3B into the same palette-shadow slots as variant A.

units.name: RefreshStagePalettePrefix
units.summary: Load the current stage palette shadows, then tail-call the three bounded alternate-palette runs. Both remain in the main bank context.

units.name: InitializePaletteAndRamTiming
units.summary: Load stage palette and alternate shadows, copy exactly 32 bytes from RamTimingAndWaitTemplate at CPU $8564 into RAM $0760..$077F and decrement RAM $0767. The template includes the $0770 wait loop; origins of unrelated RAM execution ranges remain separate questions.

units.name: LoadStagePaletteShadows
units.summary: Copies 32 stage-record bytes beginning at offset $20 into the base palette. Middle indices $0C..$17 are also replicated into both alternate shadows; the first and last portions are only stored in the base shadow.

units.name: LoadAlternatePaletteSegments
units.summary: Copies segments of the ROM data at CPU $853C into alternate palette shadows using destination shifts of zero, $0C and $18. This complements the shared middle segment loaded by the preceding routine; the ROM table itself is not classified merely by this reference.

units.name: PrepareProjectionDepth
units.summary: For nonnegative fine depth, fold into the 128-entry scale table and derive the raster-phase value before common projection arithmetic. Negative depth forms a clamped $7F projection, then adds a shared increment to the resulting fine depth and height modulo 256. The continuation is now explicit; the original quantization formula is not recovered.

units.name: ApplyProjectionScale
units.summary: Derives a coarse value from A, fetches the depth scale and multiplies it by the absolute lateral input. Preserves lateral sign separately while reducing the product, then scales height with another multiplication and a quarter-height addition. Exact fixed-point rounding, carry effects and wrap are retained. The geometric interpretation is inferred from downstream screen coordinates.

units.name: ProjectRelativeCoordinatesPrefix
units.summary: Subtract camera/progression offsets from depth, reject values outside two coarse bands and read paired 128-entry quantized tables. Multiply the lateral magnitude, reject excessive high/magnitude results and fold the accepted value around the center by side. Zero height succeeds immediately; nonzero height uses the shared multiply/shift arithmetic. Carry set rejects the coordinate, carry clear returns projected lateral/depth/height.

units.name: MultiplyUnsignedBytes
units.summary: Multiplies zero-page operands $45 and $46 by shift-and-add. Returns the 16-bit product in $48/$49; consumes the multiplier and shifts the multiplicand into $46/$47. Other projection routines reuse this scratch storage.

units.name: StartControllerFeedbackTone
units.summary: Programs pulse channel 2 with fixed control/sweep/timer values and clears three sound-envelope counters. Called on selected controller transitions; exact audible identity is unresolved.

units.name: InitializeSpriteDmaPage
units.summary: Hides sprite bytes from offset 8 onward with $FF and seeds the first two sprite records. Each sprite is Y/tile/attributes/X; the second X byte is left to later updates.

units.name: UpdateModeAndPauseInput
units.summary: Polls the controller, handles the alternate-display toggle and run-mode exit/start behavior, and uses edge counters to set a paused/control state. Starting a session selects a speed byte from button/counter conditions and re-enters screen initialization. Sound registers and queued text are adjusted on pause transitions. Specific game menu names are not established.

units.name: PollControllerEdges
units.summary: Strobes controller 1 and reads eight serial bits into the raw button byte. Merges directional state in grouped pairs; differences against the latched state increment edge counters for masks $10/$20/$40/$80, with feedback tones on the first two. Writes a phase-derived strobe afterward. Counter meanings follow their consumers rather than a universal button-name assumption.

units.name: UpdatePlayerMotionDispatch
units.summary: Clears coarse-position-change and forward-step bytes. Run mode selects an automatic step; pause/special flags can suppress updates. A transition path eases horizontal position toward $80 and elevation toward zero, then advances display/score counters. Other paths dispatch normal lateral and forward movement. The clamp and connected call continuations are now explicit under the reviewed bank contracts.

units.name: UpdateLateralMotion
units.summary: Uses raw and latched directional bits plus player flags to choose left/right movement. Updates the wrapped horizontal camera position by one or two and derives effect phase from its low six bits. In the special path also moves player horizontal position by three, clamping to $20..$DF. The shared decrement/increment entries preserve carry into the one-bit scroll high byte.

units.name: UpdateForwardProgress
units.summary: Selects a base forward step by progression index, applies temporary motion table entries or directional speed changes, and accumulates fine position modulo 64 into the coarse position. Handles coarse boundaries near $DF/$E0 and sets transition/change flags. Visible tails update mask-buffer bytes; gaps prevent a complete buffer-fill or next-stage contract.

units.name: BuildPlayerSpriteRequest
units.summary: Skips run-mode rendering, updates normal or special elevation, and derives screen X/Y. Chooses animation records from direction, elevation, state flags and frame phase, then tail-calls the metasprite decoder. A special path instead writes a four-byte render request at $0480. Exact character/animation names remain uncertain; state-driven selection is explicit.

units.name: EmitPlayerAuxiliarySpritePrefix
units.summary: For nonnegative player elevation, derive an auxiliary origin at player X+4 and Y=$B5. Emit the first sprite, then the two trailing sprites when the OAM cursor is at least eight. The common writer stores tile/attributes/Y/X, advances the cursor by four and shifts the next X left eight. Cursor zero after wrap prevents more output.

units.name: RenderPlayerQueuedRequest
units.summary: Clears the first request slot, reads its X/Y and low two style bits, selects a pointer from CPU $8C34 and tail-calls metasprite selection.

units.name: InitializeModeGraphicsPrefix
units.summary: Choose fixed-bank graphics loaders from run mode. The nonzero branch increments mode, loads alternate and supplementary graphics, then initializes multipart objects. The zero branch loads primary and supplementary graphics. Each reviewed wrapper restores mapper 6 before returning.

units.name: UpdatePlayerElevation
units.summary: Normal motion settles elevation toward zero, checks six adjacent mask-buffer entries, and starts a jump-like state from the input edge counter. State 1 uses a two-unit rise/fall with a hold threshold; states 2 and later use mirrored lookup increments and a delayed apex. Landing clears state/elevation, sets an animation timer, and programs a pulse tone. Falling past $C0 takes a session/player reset path. Jump names are inferred from elevation and input behavior.

units.name: UpdateSpecialPlayerMotion
units.summary: Dispatches by player flag bits. Table-driven arcs add or subtract elevation; thresholds clear state or invoke reset. The reset path checks the remaining-count byte, selects session restart versus player repositioning, and updates frame phase. Another state blinks display records before consuming a count and entering a recovery-like state. Exact damage/respawn semantics remain tentative.

units.name: StartJumpPulseTone
units.summary: Programs pulse channel 2 and starts a duration counter of $50; called when elevation motion begins.

units.name: AdvanceProgressionPrefix
units.summary: Advance the progression index, increment the bounded remaining counter, clear RAM $0650 and jump to the common main-screen initialization. The >=8 stage path is handled by that initializer, not by an inferred out-of-range stage record.

units.name: SelectQueuedTextPointer
units.summary: Doubles the selector in A and loads a little-endian pointer from CPU $924C into the queued-text pointer. High byte zero is used elsewhere as the empty-queue marker.

units.name: SelectPeriodicText
units.summary: Only changes queued text every 64 frame ticks. Combines the high and low tick bytes into a five-bit table index, then tail-calls text pointer selection.

units.name: SetTextNametableAddress
units.summary: Chooses nametable $2000/$2400 from a column-like coordinate, masks it to five bits, and combines row lookup bytes into a PPU address. Reads PPU status to reset the latch before writing the address.

units.name: UploadQueuedText
units.summary: When the queued pointer high byte is nonzero, consume two nametable-coordinate bytes and write characters until NUL, then clear the queued pointer high byte. Thirteen bounded ROM messages and one mutable RAM message are represented by QueuedTextPointers; not every selector is known to occur naturally.

units.name: AddDecimalDisplayValue
units.summary: Adds four contribution bytes to digit characters in $0604..$0607 with decimal carries at $3A. Propagates into $0603 and saturates trailing digits to $39 on overflow. Sets the display dirty flag. Probably score arithmetic, based on the high-water comparison and decimal representation.

units.name: UpdateDecimalHighWaterMark
units.summary: Compares the five digit characters from most to least significant. Copies the current value into $0619..$061D only when it exceeds the saved value; equality leaves the saved digits unchanged. Probably maintains the high score.

units.name: InitializeCountdownDisplay
units.summary: Copies eight template bytes to $0670 and resets an associated remaining counter and ten-tick divider.

units.name: DecrementCountdownDisplay
units.summary: Updates a pulse tone from the low counter nibble, decrements the counter, and subtracts one from a two-digit character display with borrow from $30 to $39. Increments the record dirty byte.

units.name: InitializeTimedMeter
units.summary: Copies a 16-byte display template to $0660 and seeds divider $C0 plus a signed growing meter state $80.

units.name: UpdateTimedMeter
units.summary: A signed initialization phase increases the meter every eight frame ticks up to $13 with tone feedback. The active phase counts down every $C0 eligible calls, updates a ten-byte display from lookup-selected text and blinks a sprite attribute. Expiry enters player flag $04 and requests sound $45. Paused/run/special states gate updates; the precise game resource represented by the meter is unresolved.

units.name: InitializeCurrentDisplay
units.summary: Copies nine bytes into the first display record, initializes countdown and remaining-count records, then tail-calls the 32-byte display template copy.

units.name: InitializeSavedDisplay
units.summary: Copies 16 template bytes from CPU $9627 to the second display record at $0610.

units.name: InitializeDisplayTemplate32
units.summary: Copies 32 template bytes from CPU $9637 to display records at $0620/$0630.

units.name: InitializeStatusDisplay
units.summary: Copies 16 bytes from CPU $9657 to the status record at $0640.

units.name: InitializeRemainingCount
units.summary: Copies 16 bytes from CPU $9667 to $0650 and sets the remaining-count byte to three. The counter probably represents lives, but only the bounded count mechanics are named here.

units.name: DecrementRemainingCount
units.summary: Decrements the remaining-count byte only when nonzero, marks its display dirty, and subtracts one from the corresponding decimal digit pair with borrow.

units.name: IncrementRemainingCount
units.summary: Increments the remaining-count byte only below 98 so the result stays below 99, marks the display dirty, and adds one to the decimal digit pair with carry.

units.name: ScheduleDirtyDisplayRecord
units.summary: In run mode, selects periodic text. Otherwise scans one of eight 16-byte display records per call; if dirty and the text queue is empty, queues its payload at CPU $0601 plus record offset and clears its dirty byte. Advances the rotating scan offset modulo $80.

units.name: SelectMetaspriteRecord
units.summary: Selects a little-endian metasprite pointer. The first entry indexes a two-byte table directly; the alternate entry uses groups of four frame pointers selected by the coarse projection byte, choosing CPU $C293 or $C393 by selector $20. Then enters the shared record decoder.

units.name: EmitMetaspriteRecord
units.summary: Consumes four-byte records: signed/wrapping Y delta, tile, attributes, and X delta. Deltas accumulate in the current sprite position; a leading $FF terminates successfully with carry clear. A zero next-sprite offset means no capacity; wrapping the offset after a write sets carry. Caller supplies a valid pointer and timing; no table extents beyond consumed records are inferred.

units.name: UpdateAuxiliaryEffectPrefix
units.summary: Count down a temporary palette effect, cycle its high color bits and restore stage color at completion. Dispatch normal or special auxiliary motion by player mode. The normal path starts from an input edge, reads motion tables, projects coordinates and selects a metasprite. Preserve the collision lateral value and advance its state only while unpaused; exact game-facing identity remains tentative.

units.name: UpdateSpecialAuxiliaryEffectPrefix
units.summary: Clear the second render request, start a special auxiliary state from input when allowed, and derive lateral/height inputs from player-position tables. Unless paused, decrease depth by seven until it falls below $0F. Project the remaining state, save its bounds/screen coordinates and submit the bounded overlay/render request.

units.name: RenderAuxiliaryQueuedRequest
units.summary: Clears the second queued render slot, loads its screen coordinates and style, selects a two-byte pointer from CPU $9F6D, and invokes the shared metasprite decoder.

units.name: UpdateImmediateSoundEffects
units.summary: Under low-meter conditions drives a frame-dependent triangle pitch. Advances two competing noise envelopes and a pulse-2 decay counter, writing APU control/timer registers from ROM tables or derived values. These immediate effects share pulse 2 with the sequencer; its effect-duration gate prevents premature overwrite.

units.name: UpdateProjectedObjectVariants
units.summary: Visible entries update a record phase modulo 128 or 64 and use lookup pairs, folded triangle motion or fixed coordinates as projection inputs. Calls shared object projection; carry rejects invisible objects and X distinguishes collision responses. A successful noncollision path selects metasprite $08. Gaps after response stores leave complete object-state changes unresolved.

units.name: UpdateFixedProjectedObject
units.summary: Projects fixed offsets and tests collision result X. A collision can clear the object type or enter a player flag $08 motion response with sound/delay counters; the no-collision path selects metasprite $09. Gaps in the object-clear continuation are not explained as complete behavior.

units.name: DecrementObjectTimerPrefix
units.summary: Decrement field 7. If it expires, clear the type. Fold the resulting timer into a four-entry record selector, discard one handler return frame with PLA/PLA and tail-call record selection. This is the timer exit of projection, not an ordinary return to its immediate caller.

units.name: ProjectObjectAndPrepareCollisionPrefix
units.summary: Merge object field 1 into lateral input and field 4 into coarse depth, then project relative to the camera. Reject carry-set or horizontal-overflow results. Field 7 gates a cooldown; otherwise submit the overlay and return player proximity in X or auxiliary proximity in Y, with asymmetric height bounds and ones-complement lateral distances. Exact collision response follows the caller's handler.

units.name: StartObjectHitTone
units.summary: Programs a fixed pulse-2 tone and reserves the channel for $14 ticks; called when the primary moving object is hit.

units.name: StartTrailHitTone
units.summary: Programs a different pulse-2 tone and reserves the channel for $28 ticks; called for a trailing-part hit.

units.name: UpdateObjectPaletteVariants
units.summary: Derives three palette colors from the high phase bits in object field $0395, or uses $0F for the inactive state. Replicates each color into two triplets in one of the three palette shadows.

units.name: UpdatePrimaryMovingObject
units.summary: Tracks active state and palette phase, then moves a depth-like coordinate back and forth with stage-dependent steps and accumulating fractions. Other wrapped phases select folded lookup positions. Projection produces screen coordinates; bounded three-axis difference tests detect an auxiliary-effect hit or player contact, updating player/sound flags. Stores a four-byte history entry plus a render request and manages the primary cooldown/termination. The connected hit/reinitialize continuations and sixty sprite records are now explicit; multipart game identity remains unresolved.

units.name: UpdateTrailingObjectParts
units.summary: Visits seven records at $0390..$03F0 in $10-byte strides. Delayed records decrement their activation timer. Active records retrieve a position from the circular four-byte history, append four-byte render requests, and update hit cooldowns before collision/render helpers. Unclassified cooldown tails are retained rather than invented.

units.name: TestTrailingPartContacts
units.summary: Test auxiliary and player proximity against the trailing part. Ordinary misses return to the part updater; the supported contact path can discard one caller return frame before continuing the response. This requires the nested stack contract, not a universal ordinary-RTS summary.

units.name: QueueProjectedTrailOverlay
units.summary: If alternate display is off and depth is below $40, reduces depth to a nonzero coarse code and tail-calls the three-byte overlay-list append. Otherwise returns. Includes an adjacent return stub used by request rejection.

units.name: RenderMovingObjectRequest
units.summary: Consumes a four-byte render request and clears its active/depth byte. Rejects depth outside $40 or $60 according to display mode, then selects frame pointers from depth-to-frame lookup and request style. Primary direction, alternate display, effect phase and an eight-frame animation bit choose the pointer table. Tail-calls the common metasprite decoder.

units.name: InitializeMultipartObject
units.summary: Activates the primary record, loads progression-indexed motion/appearance fields, and clears history/cooldowns. Seeds seven trailing records with active code 2, delay 8 and shared stage-selected parameters. Initializes stage palette tail fields. Records use $10-byte strides; the complete field semantics and lookup-table extents remain unresolved.

units.name: SelectSoundSequence
units.summary: A command with bit $40 selects a new sound sequence and resets the channel-init cursor. Builds a sequence-pointer-table address in CPU $D000 space, initializes one channel pair per call through ROM lookup-selected channel state, and advances the cursor by two. After four pairs, clears the request, enables the channel mask and APU channels, and resets channel state flags. The thirty-two-pointer prefix and bounded command backing are now classified separately.

units.name: SubmitSoundChannelShadows
units.summary: Handles signed sound stop commands or delegates a positive sequence command. Otherwise shifts a channel mask and submits enabled pulse/triangle/noise shadow registers. Pulse 2 honors the immediate-effect duration before sequencer writes; note flags select silence, held volume, or new timer values. Two logical pulse-2 shadows are visited sequentially, so later enabled writes can supersede earlier ones.

units.name: AdvanceSoundChannelEnvelopes
units.summary: Iterates five logical channel states: 12 bytes per zero-page state and 16 bytes per register shadow. For enabled channels, decrements note duration; expiry decodes the next command. Otherwise advances a fractional envelope index, clamps it to 15, and reads a volume byte through the channel envelope pointer into its shadow.

units.name: DecodeSoundCommand
units.summary: Read channel stream bytes until emitting a note/rest or requesting stop. Below $C0 selects pitch and duration; $C0..$CF emits rests; $D0..$D7 performs a counted branch with a two-byte target; $D8..$DF selects pitch; $E0..$EF selects envelope. $F8 consumes a rate parameter, $F9..$FE selects duration backing and $FF requests global stop. Other high commands advance one byte. This mechanical grammar does not prove full natural command usage or complete song-table schema.

units.name: StartSoundNoteOrRest
units.summary: The note entry saves the command, loads pitch, then sets duration from its low nibble. The rest entry sets duration and marks the channel shadow flag $80 without loading pitch.

units.name: LoadSoundPitch
units.summary: For logical noise state, derive period from the note high nibble plus four and mark its shadow for reload. Other states index two-byte timers with an even offset 0..30 and store new-note status $7F. Pitch backing remains generic where its full selector/table organization is unresolved.

units.name: LoadSoundDuration
units.summary: Indexes the channel duration table by low command nibble, writes the countdown and resets envelope index/fraction.

units.name: SelectSoundDurationTable
units.summary: Derives a 16-byte duration-table pointer in the CPU $BBE0 area from the command. Exact carry arithmetic is retained; no inferred table extent is added to classification.

units.name: SelectSoundPitchTable
units.summary: Uses the command low three bits to choose a pitch-table offset. Higher channel-state offsets reduce/clamp the selector before deriving a pointer from CPU $BAF6 plus the offset lookup.

units.name: SelectSoundEnvelopeTable
units.summary: Shifts the command into a 16-byte envelope selector, adds the CPU $BC50 base and stores the channel envelope pointer. Carry supplies the pointer high byte.

units.name: DispatchObjectAndOverlayUpdates
units.summary: Clear the three-byte overlay list and dispatch object updates from transition, run mode and player flags. Main-bank auxiliary/object routines and fixed render-request routines use reviewed bank-preserving or mapper-6-restoring contracts. Remaining mixed fragments are local structural questions; no blanket post-call unknown assumption is needed.

units.name: SelectPaletteVariantAPrefix
units.summary: Copy stage palette variant A, preserve the previous display tile, set tile $42 and mark the record dirty. Convert the first counter minus two through the shared numeric display helper. The connected display-helper continuations are now explicit.

units.name: SelectPaletteVariantBPrefix
units.summary: Copy stage palette variant B, restore the saved display tile, mark the record dirty and convert the second counter minus two through the same helper. The copied palette fields are stage-record fields, not separate graphics-bank execution.

units.name: InitializeObjectProgressPrefix
units.summary: In run mode seeds coarse/fine progression and clears the line-mask buffer. Otherwise chooses an initial object stream from checkpoint-like state and calls the stream loader. Visible alternate entries seed change counters; gaps prevent a complete checkpoint/initialization contract.

units.name: VisitObjectRecordPage
units.summary: Derives one of four $40-byte object pages in RAM $0500 and visits sixteen $10-byte records through the shared object handler. Pointer low-byte wrapping is intentional; X/Y are scratch in the callee.

units.name: DispatchObjectRecord
units.summary: Skips record type zero. Otherwise decrements type into a two-byte handler-pointer index at CPU $A07B. Chooses a motion step from run speed unless paused/cooldown, reads field $0C into A, and jumps indirectly through $0047. This is a handler contract, not proof that every table entry is code.

units.name: RotatePalettePrefix
units.summary: Every fourth frame swap the first two bytes of each palette pair at RAM offsets $070A, $072A and $074A. The helper saves byte zero, moves byte one into its place, then restores the saved byte into slot one. This is a two-byte swap, not an initialization or rotation of an unknown-length record.

units.name: UpdateVerticalTransition
units.summary: Uses flag bit $40 to choose elevation increase or decrease. At the $C0 threshold flips the phase and selects a palette variant; the reverse path clamps at zero, clears player motion flags and requests a progression-dependent sound. Both paths return to the object-page visit.

units.name: LoadStageObjectGroups
units.summary: Dispatch vertical transition or active object-page updates. On coarse-position change, build a sixteen-byte RAM-record pointer in $05xx and a stage-grid pointer, rotate the page selector modulo four and fetch four type bytes. For each type, select mapper 0 to read its grid byte, restore mapper 6, parse it and advance the record cursor by $10. Stage<8 selects one of eight 1 KiB grids. Parser writes remain in the sixteen-byte RAM record; this does not establish all type meanings or natural selector use.

units.name: PrepareObjectCollisionMaskPrefix
units.summary: Derive a collision mask from reverse/forward flags and object coarse position. For one or six consecutive depth samples, call the bounded relative-depth lookup; on success store the mask in RAM $06C0+projected depth. Increment fine depth modulo 64 and propagate wrap into coarse depth between samples. This explains the buffer mechanics without inventing a complete collision-map schema.

units.name: AppendOverlayTriplet
units.summary: Returns immediately for coarse code zero. Otherwise appends screen Y derived from depth plus $79, lateral position, and coarse code to the three-byte list at $0400, advances its byte offset and writes a zero terminator. The routine has no capacity guard; callers must bound list size.

units.name: RenderOverlayTriplets
units.summary: Reads zero-terminated three-byte overlay records. Each becomes two sprites sharing Y/tile with X separated by eight pixels and attributes $41/$01. Stops if sprite byte offset is below eight or a record terminator is reached. The local X advances without updating the global sprite cursor in this visible routine.

units.name: AlternateOverlayAndPlayerAuxiliary
units.summary: Skips work in alternate-display mode. Otherwise alternates between player auxiliary sprites and overlay triplets using frame-tick parity.

units.name: RenderRequestsByDepth
units.summary: Optionally clear player/auxiliary requests in run mode, then repeatedly scan four-byte render requests for greatest nonzero depth. Dispatch player, auxiliary or moving-object rendering by slot; consumers clear request markers so later scans progress. The finite object, pose and action dispatch contracts and mapper-restoring wrappers remain explicit.

units.name: GraphicsLoaderEntryTable
units.summary: Three jump entries dispatch stage graphics, alternate graphics and supplementary stage data loaders. Callers must account for mapper writes and fixed-bank execution.

units.name: LoadPrimaryStageGraphics
units.summary: Disable rendering, set source high=$80+8*stage for stage<8, select mapper 3 (physical banks 6/7) and upload eight pages to PPU $1800. Restore mapper 6 before returning. PrimaryStagePatternSets is the coherent eight-set backing; the fixed code remains visible during both mapper changes.

units.name: LoadAlternateGraphics
units.summary: Disables rendering, forms a progression-indexed CPU source pointer, switches the lower PRG window to mapper value 2, and uploads eight pages at PPU $1800. Restores mapper value 6 before returning. Effective physical banks are pairs 4/5 and 12/13 for those values, not mapper values used as bank indices.

units.name: LoadSupplementaryStageGraphics
units.summary: Disable rendering and select mapper 0 for stage-indexed four-page supplementary patterns at PPU $0C00. Select mapper 4 for two successive one-page nametable uploads at $2100/$2D00, then restore mapper 6. Copy two sixteen-byte stage attribute fragments through PPU $23D0/$2FD0 and reset scroll. Known source/count contracts bound the pattern and row backing; complete stage-field game meaning remains uncertain.

units.name: WaitForNmiReturn
units.summary: Clears the stack-page NMI mode byte, enables NMI using the PPU-control shadow, and loops forever locally. The fixed-bank NMI handler discards its interrupt frame and returns through the caller stack instead of RTI. This nonlocal return is an intentional calling convention; do not model the loop as a normal subroutine return.

units.name: EnterMainBankWithResetMarker
units.summary: Stores reset marker $35 in StartupMarker and jumps to lower-window CPU $8000. The preceding reset path selects mapper 6, giving physical PRG banks 12/13 for that entry.

units.name: ResetAndSelectSessionBank
units.summary: Disable interrupts/rendering and decimal mode, wait for three vblank status observations, initialize controller/APU/stack and inspect marker RAM $0102. Marker $35 selects mapper 6 and jumps to main startup; marker $36 selects mapper 4 and jumps to the bank8 scene. Otherwise call CPU $8000 under mapper 1 then mapper 5, load startup graphics, restore mapper 6 and enter main startup. CPU aliases are resolved by those effective bank contexts; vector reachability alone proves no normal ending route.

units.name: LoadStartupGraphics
units.summary: Under the established banks 10/11 entry contract, disable rendering and copy 32 pages of StartupPatternSet from CPU $A000 to PPU $0000. Then copy eight pages of StartupNametableSource from $9800 to PPU $2000 through the shared page copier. The loader does not choose its own PRG bank; other entry contexts cannot be assumed to use the same physical backing.

units.name: CopyPagesToPpu
units.summary: A supplies PPU destination high byte, destination low byte is zero. Copies X pages of 256 bytes from the zero-page source pointer, advancing only its high byte. PPU status resets the address latch; caller controls rendering and mapping. X zero would wrap through 256 pages, so callers supply a nonzero bounded count.

units.name: NmiStackDispatch
units.summary: Tests NmiReturnMode sign. Negative mode jumps indirectly through the installed callback pointer without saving registers. Nonnegative mode restores PPU control, reads PPU status, sets mode $FF, discards three interrupt-stack bytes and executes RTS to the waiting caller. This handler deliberately substitutes a caller return for the ordinary interrupt return; hardware correctness beyond the observed contract is not asserted.

units.name: InitializeDormantPpuFragment
units.summary: Rendering mask is supplied in A. With banks 2/3 mapped, copy three pages from $8100 to PPU $0000, then four from the advanced $8400 pointer to $2000. Install the local palette and finish with a nested software delay. No natural entry into this fragment is established; the leading byte remains unknown.

units.name: InstallDormantPalette
units.summary: Write sixteen local palette bytes to $3F00, reset the palette/address latch and scroll, wait for vblank, then enable the background mask $0A. This initializer uses its own palette and graphics, separate from the running-game loaders.

units.name: CopyDormantPagesToPpu
units.summary: A supplies destination high, low is zero; X is a nonzero page count. Copy from ($00),Y to PPU data, advancing source high on each Y wrap. Return with X zero and the source at the following page. Caller must keep banks 2/3 mapped.

units.name: RunBank8AnimationSequence
units.summary: Continue scene setup after the reviewed initializer, hide OAM, request sound $41 and run palette, character and segmented-object animation phases. The final loop waits through the fixed NMI service and ticks this bank's sound driver. Entry/return safety depends on the saved artificial SP=$F8 contract; this is not proof of normal ending completion.

units.name: TickBank8Scene
units.summary: Wait for NMI, upload sprite palette and DMA page $02, then hide the next OAM buffer and reset its cursor. Tick sound and advance the scene frame counter. The wait service deliberately returns through the NMI stack contract, not an ordinary interrupt return.

units.name: RunBank8RisingEffect
units.summary: Draw the hero and an auxiliary record for 79 frames. The auxiliary X advances with the local phase; Y is hero Y minus $17. This is a scene-specific placement effect.

units.name: RunBank8HeroTravel
units.summary: Align and step hero X, move to $F4, wait 128 ticks, then move from X=$0C to $3C. The helper compares X to a target byte; its CMP carry deliberately controls the signed direction of ADC #1.

units.name: RunBank8SegmentAnimation
units.summary: For the current selector, load per-object configuration and initialize four vertical segment positions to $F0. Draw hero plus four parts; move the first part upward by two every fourth tick until below $8A. Then run a 32-step hold, a 32-step pose cycle, and a downward exit. Exact character identities are uncertain.

units.name: RunEightBank8SegmentAnimations
units.summary: Run the segmented animation once for each selector 0..7.

units.name: AnimateBank8PaletteRamp
units.summary: Carry chooses one of two four-entry palette ramps. Over 32 scene ticks, DMA OAM, upload palettes, tick sound and select a palette byte every eight ticks. The fixed wait helper preserves banks 8/9 under the reviewed entry contract.

units.name: AnimateBank8PaletteTriples
units.summary: Over 72 ticks, select nine four-byte records with frame/8 and copy the first three bytes into palette slots 1..3. The fourth record byte is not consumed here.

units.name: ContinueBank8SceneSeed
units.summary: Finish the backward scene seed-table copy, then initialize the palette and upload sixteen pattern pages. The indexed zero-page stores preserve the mapper.

units.name: TickBank8Sound
units.summary: Scene-local entry into a second sound engine. It shares the twelve-byte zero-page channel format and $0300 shadow records with the main-bank driver, but uses its own ROM tables under banks 8/9. Do not resolve its $9Axx data through the main-bank CPU alias.

units.name: DispatchBank8SoundCommand
units.summary: Negative command $80 silences the APU and advances to $81; other negative commands return. Positive commands initialize stream pointers. Zero performs the regular shadow flush and envelope/channel update.

units.name: EnterSceneAfterFinalStage
units.summary: For progression index >=8, tail-jump to the fixed mapper-4 selection entry and enter the bank8 scene at CPU $8000. This path does not return through the main-bank initializer or establish natural ending completion.

units.name: MarkTimedMeterAndQueueSound
units.summary: Set the meter dirty bit, queue sound $44 and join the common initialization path.

units.name: BeginMainRunState
units.summary: Clear special motion, center the player, advance the run state and call the fixed display updater before the common setup continuation.

units.name: JoinMainStateInitialization
units.summary: Join the shared state initialization without changing the bank.

units.name: ResetMainRunWorkingState
units.summary: Clear auxiliary/effect state and seed the same two stage-record fields into three render records. Select special-motion state 1, run the object initializer and graphics wrapper, then restore the PPU mode. Stage fields $31/$32 are copied mechanically; their full game meaning remains unresolved.

units.name: InitializeMainPpuThroughWrapper
units.summary: The fixed graphics wrapper returns with mapper 6; continue with the running-game display mask and control.

units.name: JoinMainPaletteSetup
units.summary: Jump into the existing palette setup continuation after the reviewed call return.

units.name: ApplySharedCoordinateIncrement
units.summary: Add the same modulo-256 increment to projection fine depth and height, then return. The increment's interpretation depends on the caller.

units.name: FinishProjectionLateralAndHeight
units.summary: Consume the multiplication result in $48/$49 to form a lateral magnitude. Reject values beyond the supported 16-unit high-part or $78 output bound with carry set; otherwise fold the sign into the center-relative coordinate. Height zero succeeds immediately; positive height continues through the scaled height calculation.

units.name: NormalizeProjectionRelativeDepth
units.summary: Subtract the reference fine/coarse depth, wrap fine depth to six bits and reject negative or >=2 coarse differences. Combine coarse bit and fine depth into a 0..127 lookup index; replace fine depth with the quantized value and return carry clear.

units.name: ContinueObjectMotionAfterCall
units.summary: Rejoin the existing motion routine after its reviewed mapper-preserving call.

units.name: ContinueAuxiliaryMotionAfterCall
units.summary: Continue the established auxiliary motion branch without another bank transition.

units.name: FinishRasterTailFill
units.summary: Finish the raster-buffer fill through index $3F and return. The indexed RAM write cannot change the mapper.

units.name: FinishRasterSplitFill
units.summary: Finish the first run up to its requested limit, then fill the remaining raster slots through $3F with the complemented value. Skip the tail when the first run already reaches 64.

units.name: EmitTwoTrailingRasterSprites
units.summary: When OAM cursor is at least eight, emit tile $FF one row lower, restore Y, then emit tile $FD. These are trailing raster sprites with attribute 1; the exact visual role of those tile IDs remains uncertain.

units.name: FinishSingleRasterSprite
units.summary: Complete the four-byte OAM entry, advance the OAM cursor by four and move the next X position left by eight. The tile was written by the preceding shared entry.

units.name: LoadGraphicsThroughFixedWrapper
units.summary: Tail-call the fixed graphics wrapper, whose reviewed contract restores mapper 6 before returning to the original caller.

units.name: FinishProgressionAdvance
units.summary: Clear RAM $0650 and rejoin the ordinary main-loop continuation.

units.name: QueueStageAndValueTextDigits
units.summary: Convert A and the progression index into tile codes by adding $31; store them in the display record and set its dirty flag. This is the parser helper used by object types $58..$5C; it writes only $0640/$0649/$064D.

units.name: RenderProjectedVerticalObject
units.summary: Use record field $0F and projected depth to select upper/lower tiles and height-dependent row counts. Emit paired, oppositely flipped sprites for wider depth values; narrow depth uses a single column shifted left four. Draw the upper portion upward, reset to the saved baseline, and draw the lower portion downward. OAM cursor wrap stops rendering.

units.name: QueueObjectContactSound
units.summary: Reset motion phase and queue sound $45 for this contact path.

units.name: CheckAuxiliaryObjectContact
units.summary: If an auxiliary object exists, compare fine depth to its half-open interval and lateral ones-complement distance against nine. A match clears its active state and primary noise, then starts secondary noise. Continue with the object's per-record phase accumulation when applicable.

units.name: PrepareProjectedObjectScreenOrigin
units.summary: Set upper Y=fine depth+$79, saved lower baseline from height subtraction and the carry-dependent +7, and X=lateral+scroll. Tail-call the vertical-object renderer.

units.name: RenderAuxiliaryObjectFrame
units.summary: Project the auxiliary origin, preserve its collision lateral value, select a metasprite through the auxiliary-state lookup and advance its state only when not paused. Tail-call the established record emitter.

units.name: QueueProjectedRenderRequest
units.summary: Save auxiliary depth/lateral bounds, calculate screen coordinates with the alternate-display scroll mask, write the four-byte request at $0484 and request eight output units. Continue through the fixed render-request copier.

units.name: TestPlayerAndAuxiliaryProximity
units.summary: Return separate proximity results: X=1/2 distinguishes the player elevation side inside the center lane, and Y=1 reports the auxiliary depth/lateral interval case. Default X/Y are zero and carry is clear. Player comparisons use asymmetric height bounds $0D/$20 and ones-complement magnitude; exact gameplay purpose remains tentative.

units.name: AdvanceObjectPaletteCountdown
units.summary: Decrement the object timer; a negative result starts the staggered object pulse sequence. Otherwise use timer bits 2..4 to copy three consecutive stage palette bytes from fields $50 onward and continue the existing object updater.

units.name: RestoreObjectCountdownFromStack
units.summary: Pop the previously saved value, subtract one into RAM $0394 and mark the meter dirty. This is a continuation with a caller-supplied stack byte, not a free-standing ordinary entry.

units.name: FinishObjectRewardBranch
units.summary: Retain the incoming zero flag: a nonzero result takes the existing alternate path. Otherwise saturate RAM $0384 upward by eight, clear the indexed object active byte and return.

units.name: AdvanceObjectPulseCountdown
units.summary: Decrement the indexed object timer. At zero start pulse decay, set the object phase to $7F, complement the shared lateral byte, clear its auxiliary flag and forward stored coordinates to the existing helper. A nonzero timer returns unchanged.

units.name: StartStaggeredObjectPulse
units.summary: Queue sound $46 only when RAM $0394 is zero, then start noise/decay and seed eight object phases from $F8 down to $C0 in steps of eight. Prepare the coordinate helper inputs exactly as stored; $74 is intentionally overwritten with zero before the tail call, so no X-coordinate preservation is claimed.

units.name: ResumeMainSoundCommandParser
units.summary: Resume the existing main-bank sound parser after a reviewed helper return; effective banks remain 12/13/14/15.

units.name: HandleMainSoundLoop
units.summary: Command $D0..$D7 uses the low nibble as the loop-counter seed. If the shadow loop counter is zero, seed it and branch through the following little-endian pointer. Otherwise decrement: reaching zero skips three bytes; a still-nonzero counter branches. Both saved and working stream pointers are updated. Natural command use/frequency is unresolved.

units.name: FinishMainSoundPitchReload
units.summary: Mark the selected shadow with positive status $7F so the next APU flush reloads its timer.

units.name: CallMainObjectUpdaterFromFixedBank
units.summary: The fixed-bank caller enters the main object updater under banks 12/13/14/15. The reviewed return graph preserves that mapper context.

units.name: PrepareFirstDisplayCounter
units.summary: Save the previous display tile, write tile $42 and mark the record dirty. Convert the first counter minus two through the shared numeric display helper.

units.name: PrepareSecondDisplayCounter
units.summary: Restore the saved tile, mark the record dirty again and convert the second counter minus two through the same helper.

units.name: SwapAdditionalPalettePairs
units.summary: Swap the additional palette pairs at RAM $072A and $074A after the first pair has been processed. The common helper exchanges exactly two bytes in each selected pair.

units.name: FinishPalettePairSwap
units.summary: Finish the two-byte palette swap: put the saved original byte zero into slot one and return. The pair address is $0700+X and is always RAM.

units.name: ReadObjectTypeAndRestoreMainBank
units.summary: Fetch the stage-grid type with mapper 0 active, then use X=6 to restore physical banks 12/13 before parsing it. The fixed code stays visible throughout. Process the record, advance stream coordinate and RAM-record cursor by $10, and repeat the bounded group count.

units.name: ParseStageObjectType
units.summary: The type byte selects empty, ordinary, special-state or compound object handling. The established calling contract points $61/$62 into $05xx RAM with Y<=15. Zero clears field 0; types below $30 initialize ordinary records; $60..$BF build compound records. Other ranges update state or delegate before clearing. Natural selector coverage is separate from this bounded parser mechanics.

units.name: ClearHighObjectTypeRecord
units.summary: Types $C0..$DF clear this record through the shared zero initializer; no executable payload is inferred from the type value.

units.name: TestSpecialObjectType
units.summary: Compare the stage threshold against $E0; below it substitute ordinary type $2E, otherwise match the active selector before changing player-state high bits.

units.name: QueueObjectTypeMessage
units.summary: Types $58..$5C become digit-like display values through the bounded helper; set a two-tick marker relative to RAM $34 and mark the timed meter dirty, then clear this object record.

units.name: InitializeOrdinaryObjectRecord
units.summary: Store the ordinary type into field 0 with caller Y=0, then continue through FinishOrdinaryParsedRecord. That tail sets fields 1/4/7 and toggles field $0C; no initial value for $0C is assumed.

units.name: InitializeCompoundObjectRecord
units.summary: Preserve the type in X and set base type $2F. Store depth/flags, lateral position and the type low nibble. Reduce ($60..$BF)-$60 by four shifts to select six-entry field tables for offsets 5, 6 and $0F; clear field 8. If field $0F is nonzero, fold the low subtype bits into field 1. All writes remain in the caller's sixteen-byte RAM record.

units.name: AdvanceCollisionMaskDepth

units.name: RamTimingAndWaitTemplate
units.summary: Exactly 32 bytes copied from CPU $8564 into RAM $0760..$077F by the main initializer, followed by a patch to RAM $0767. units.name: ProjectionFineLookup
units.summary: 128 quantized fine-depth values. The relative-depth helper accepts two coarse bands and a six-bit fine component, producing the bounded index 0..127. Values belong to the consumer representation; no original generator/rounding algorithm is asserted.

units.name: ProjectionCoarseLookup

units.name: ProjectionScaleLookup

units.name: StageForwardStep

units.name: Noncode_019002

units.name: JumpState2Increments

units.name: JumpLaterStateIncrements

units.name: Noncode_0190E2
units.summary: A bounded 65-byte monotone curve with values 0..127 between known motion/delay bases. Neighboring consumers and raw progression were inspected, but the exact curve role and generating formula remain unresolved.

units.name: Noncode_019123

units.name: PeriodicTextSelectors

units.name: QueuedTextMessages

Historical PLACE SIDE A/B strings are present as bytes; their appearance does not prove disk hardware support or natural display in this cartridge.

units.name: QueuedTextPointers

units.name: NametableRowAddressLow

units.name: NametableRowAddressHigh

units.name: DisplayRecordTemplates

units.name: SoundDurationAndRateTables

units.name: SoundEnvelopeTables
units.summary: Sixteen sixteen-sample volume envelopes selected by commands $E0..$EF. The envelope clock retains a four-bit fraction and clamps sample index to 15; all samples are 0..15. These are main-bank tables, separate from the bank8 sound-driver backing.

units.name: Bank6MetaspritePointerPrefix

units.name: Bank6AndFixedMetaspriteRecords

Each record is four-byte (deltaY,tile,attributes,deltaX) tuples, terminated by $FF at a tuple boundary; lengths are at most 61 bytes. Relative coordinates accumulate modulo 256 in EmitMetaspriteRecord. Under banks 12/13/14/15 the $BFFF->$C000 crossing enters fixed bank14 continuously. Exact end is the independent $C293 pointer backing.
