units.name: AppendLegacySceneFollower
units.summary: Load follower-three coordinates into the drawing accumulator and append the selected scene record. This coherent wrapper starts after the unresolved truncated byte at $8600.

units.name: HideLegacySceneOam
units.summary: Hide all 64 OAM slots by writing Y=$F4 at every fourth byte of page $02. The X wrap ends the loop.

units.name: UploadLegacyScenePalette
units.summary: Transfer sixteen sprite-palette bytes from scene RAM to PPU $3F10, reset the address latch and scroll, and disable PPU control. Rendering must already be disabled or the caller must supply a safe PPU access interval.

units.name: InitializeLegacySceneGraphics
units.summary: Copy sixteen bytes of the code at $8018 into RAM $50..$5F, then install the local sixteen-byte palette. The seed source remains Code despite this read. Upload sixteen pages from $A000 into PPU $0000 under banks 8/9; finish with control and scroll zero. The inline palette at $864A separates these code bodies.

units.name: LegacySceneRecordDone
units.summary: Return when the tuple-boundary terminator is reached.

units.name: AppendLegacySceneRecord
units.summary: For a supported scene selector, read its pointer and append four-byte (deltaY,tile,attributes,deltaX) tuples to OAM. Coordinates accumulate modulo 256; $FF ends a record only in the deltaY position. Stop also when adding four wraps the OAM cursor. This duplicate helper uses the same bounded scene record backing as the active renderer.

units.name: StartPresentationDelay
units.summary: Seed the presentation software countdown with $C8 and fall into its established delay loop. This is a local delay, not a frame count.

units.name: SelectPresentationPalette
units.summary: Point $EE/$EF at the sixteen-byte palette at $81CC and fall into the existing palette uploader under banks 10/11.

units.name: JoinTransitionWait
units.summary: Join the existing RAM $0770 wait-call path. Its uploaded template loops at $0770; this continuation does not prove a return into the following isolated RTS.

units.name: JoinElevationClamp
units.summary: Continue the player update through the signed elevation clamp.

units.name: ClampPlayerElevation
units.summary: When player flags are zero and either controller bit $04/$08 is set, adjust elevation by three. Bit $04 selects subtraction with a floor of zero; otherwise addition clamps negative overflow to $7F. Other inputs leave elevation unchanged.

units.name: ReadPpuStatus
units.summary: Read PPU status into A and return, including its normal latch-reset side effect.

units.name: IncrementBoundedDisplayCount
units.summary: Increase the internal count only below 99. Advance the rightmost display character through 9; on rollover replace it with 0 and increment the preceding character. Mark the display record dirty after either update.

units.name: StoreObjectHeightPhase
units.summary: Store the prepared projection height in field $0E of the active $63/$64 RAM record, then continue the existing moving-object path.

units.name: FinishVerticalObjectProjection
units.summary: Save projected motion depth; negative results clear object fields 7/8. Otherwise derive sprite Y from its complement and test the narrow player lateral/height window. A hit invokes the six-action dispatcher; a miss chooses the field-7-dependent record. All indirect writes require the active RAM-record contract.

units.name: DispatchObjectContactAction
units.summary: Require object field 7 in 1..6. Convert it to a zero-based word index, clear fields 7/8, seed the pulse-2 contact tone and jump through the six-word action table. The contract is conditional; arbitrary record values do not establish a larger dispatch table.

units.name: SetTimedMeterHighBit
units.summary: Set the high bit of the timed meter value.

units.name: StartContactPaletteEffect
units.summary: Derive palette-effect cycles from player elevation, clear its tick, enable the effect and queue sound $43.

units.name: StartContactMotion
units.summary: If the palette effect is inactive, reset jump motion, seed phase $0C and flags $04, and queue sound $45.

units.name: ToggleContactPaletteState
units.summary: On first selection set the contact flag and palette shadows to $16; later selections submit the shared numeric-display update.

units.name: EnableAlternateContactState
units.summary: Set the second contact flag once; subsequent calls use the same display-update continuation.

units.name: QueueContactPlayerRecord
units.summary: Tail-call the established player record selector.

units.name: EmptyObjectHandler
units.summary: Return for the empty handler entry.

units.name: HandleLowFixedObject
units.summary: Project centered lateral input with zero height and fine depth; join the shared proximity response.

units.name: HandleMidFixedObject
units.summary: Use height $19 with centered lateral input and zero fine depth.

units.name: HandleHighFixedObject
units.summary: Use height $3F with centered lateral input and zero fine depth.

units.name: HandleRaisedFixedObject
units.summary: Use height $30 with centered lateral input and zero fine depth.

units.name: RespondToFixedObjectProximity
units.summary: Project and test proximity. On accepted player contact seed an eight-tick object timer, delay forward motion, add the display increment and play the short tone. Then render record 8. Projection may return normally or abort this handler through its timer contract.

units.name: HandleShortVerticalWave
units.summary: Advance the record phase by the motion step modulo 32, fold it to a triangle and add $30 to height before the existing variant response.

units.name: HandleTallVerticalWave
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 128 and fold height at 64; project at centered lateral position. Accepted contact sets the same delay, timer, display increment and tone before record 8.

units.name: FinishVariantContact
units.summary: Apply the display increment and short contact tone, then join the record-8 continuation.

units.name: HandleStateChangingObject
units.summary: Project a fixed low raised object. On contact clear its type, reset motion, set flags $C0 and save object/stage positions. Seed the direct pulse effect and queue sound $80; without contact render record 7.

units.name: AddObjectDisplayIncrement
units.summary: Submit the shared numeric-display increment with five in its low component, then increment the bounded count display.

units.name: StartJumpStateTwoFromObject
units.summary: Complete the contact clear by resetting phase/fall state, selecting jump state 2 and joining the shared pulse tone.

units.name: HandleHorizontalWaveContact
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 128 and fold lateral input into 0..63. Reuse the fixed-object proximity response at fine depth $20 and zero height.

units.name: HandleRaisedJumpContact
units.summary: Set height $14 and centered coordinates before the common jump response.

units.name: HandleGroundJumpContact
units.summary: Set zero height and centered coordinates before the common jump response.

units.name: RespondWithJumpStateThree
units.summary: Project and test player contact. Contact class 1 clears the object and selects jump state 3; another nonzero class uses the existing delayed-motion response. No contact renders record $0A.

units.name: PlayJumpContactTone
units.summary: Write the four pulse-2 registers and hold the immediate effect for $50 ticks.

units.name: PlayShortObjectTone
units.summary: Write the short pulse-2 contact tone and hold it for $28 ticks.

units.name: HandleCameraAlignedObject
units.summary: Clamp the camera-relative lateral component to the current coarse band, use zero height and fine depth $20, then test proximity. With contact and no forward delay, seed the delayed player motion response; otherwise render record $0B.

units.name: HandleElevationAlignedObject
units.summary: Clamp negative player elevation according to jump/flag state, halve it into projection height and reuse the camera-aligned handler.

units.name: HandleFoldedLateralObject
units.summary: Advance and halve the phase, fold lateral motion into 0..63 and choose pose 0 with display increment 1.

units.name: ProjectAndDispatchObjectPose
units.summary: Require the active RAM record and pose selector below 15. Project first; an auxiliary hit clears its state and starts a longer object timer, while player contact selects the motion/palette or numeric-display response. No contact dispatches the selected pose. The projection timer may discard one nested handler frame; callers that save auxiliary state resume at their enclosing restoration continuation.

units.name: DispatchObjectPose
units.summary: Double the bounded pose selector, read one of fifteen target words and jump through the scratch pointer. Immediate producers support 0..14; no universal runtime selector-domain claim follows.

units.name: HandleHeightTrianglePose
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 64 and fold height at 32. Use centered coordinates, pose 1 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleLateralTrianglePose
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 128 and fold lateral position at 64. Use height 1, fine depth $20, pose 0 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleHighLateralTrianglePose
units.summary: Halve the byte phase and fold lateral position at 64. Use height $1F, fine depth $20, pose 1 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleWidePairedPath
units.summary: Use the even phase byte as a paired-coordinate index; assign depth then lateral, height $14, pose 2 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleLowPairedPath
units.summary: Use the same paired-coordinate path at height $0A, pose 2 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleQuarterPhaseCurve
units.summary: Fold phase divided by four into 0..31. Add $10 to the phase-derived depth and curve-derived lateral coordinate; use height 1, pose 3 and increment 1.

units.name: FinishFrameGatedPath
units.summary: Advance the saved phase by motion-step bits selected by the frame counter. Fold its magnitude, derive depth and a triangular lateral coordinate, then use pose 3 with increment 1.

units.name: HandleThreeQuarterCyclePath
units.summary: Advance phase modulo $C0, halve it and read parallel lateral/depth curves. Use height 1, pose 4 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleSplitHeightCurve
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 64. The first half reads a height curve and chooses pose 14; the folded second half uses zero height and pose 5. Both use fine depth $20 and increment 2.

units.name: HandleNinetySixStepCurve
units.summary: Advance phase within 0..95, fold its second half and read height/lateral curves. Use fine depth $20, pose 5 and increment 1.

units.name: HandleProgressRelativePath
units.summary: Fold the half-phase lateral input; use inverted fine progression when the object coarse band matches, otherwise depth $3F. Choose pose 7 and increment 2.

units.name: HandleNestedHeightTriangle
units.summary: Fold the half-phase lateral input, fold it again into 0..31 and look up height. Choose fine depth $20, pose 6 and increment 2.

units.name: HandlePairedPathWithHeight
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 128, read paired lateral/depth coordinates and derive a folded complementary height. Choose pose 8 and increment 4.

units.name: HandleFineProgressPath
units.summary: Fold lateral phase and use inverted fine progression in the matching coarse band. Choose height 1, pose 10 and increment 2.

units.name: HandleHalfPhaseWithoutAuxiliary
units.summary: Use half-phase folded lateral input, height 1, fine depth $20, pose 9 and increment 4. Save auxiliary state on the stack, suppress it during the shared handler and restore it at the enclosing continuation, including supported one-frame aborts.

units.name: HandleFullPhaseWithoutAuxiliary
units.summary: Use the modulo-128 lateral triangle with the same temporary auxiliary suppression and restoration as the preceding handler.

units.name: HandleHalfPhaseProgressHeight
units.summary: Fold half-phase lateral input and derive depth/height from inverted fine progression in the matching band; otherwise use $3F/$1F. Choose pose 11 and increment 2.

units.name: HandleFullPhaseProgressHeight
units.summary: Use the modulo-128 lateral triangle and the same progress-dependent depth/height rule. Choose pose 12 and increment 4.

units.name: SelectPoseOnePath
units.summary: Select pose 1 and increment 1 before the common full-phase progression path.

units.name: SelectPoseTwoPath
units.summary: Select pose 2 and increment 1 before the common path.

units.name: SelectPoseFourPath
units.summary: Select pose 4 and increment 2 before the common path.

units.name: SelectPoseSixPath
units.summary: Select pose 6 and increment 2 before the common path.

units.name: SelectPoseThirteenPath
units.summary: Select pose 13 and increment 4 before the common path.

units.name: HandleDirectProgressPath
units.summary: Advance phase modulo 128 and fold lateral input. Use the direct fine progression in the matching coarse band, zero otherwise; height is 1. The entry wrapper supplies pose and display increment.

units.name: DecrementObjectTimerAndAbort
units.summary: Decrement field 7. If it expires, clear the type. Fold the resulting timer into a four-entry record selector, discard one handler return frame with PLA/PLA and tail-call record selection. This is the timer exit of projection, not an ordinary return to its immediate caller.

units.name: ProjectObjectAndTestContacts
units.summary: Require $63/$64 to address the active RAM record; this is separate from the parser pointer $61/$62. Merge record lateral/depth fields, project and test player/auxiliary proximity. Projection rejection returns carry set; ordinary contact tests return carry clear with X/Y categories. Nonzero field 7 instead enters the timer path, which discards one caller-handler return frame.

units.name: SelectAnimatedRecord10
units.summary: Choose animation base $10 and join the two-frame phase selector.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord12
units.summary: Choose record base $12 and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: SelectObjectRecord14
units.summary: Tail-call record selection with selector $14; no phase increment is performed in this wrapper.

units.name: SelectObjectRecord16
units.summary: Tail-call record selection with selector $16; no phase increment is performed in this wrapper.

units.name: SelectObjectRecord17
units.summary: Tail-call record selection with selector $17; no phase increment is performed in this wrapper.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord18
units.summary: Choose record base $18 and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord1A
units.summary: Choose record base $1A and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord1C
units.summary: Choose record base $1C and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: SelectObjectRecord1E
units.summary: Tail-call record selection with selector $1E; no phase increment is performed in this wrapper.

units.name: SelectObjectRecord24
units.summary: Tail-call record selection with selector $24; no phase increment is performed in this wrapper.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord26
units.summary: Choose record base $26 and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: AnimateObjectRecord28
units.summary: Choose record base $28 and join the common two-frame phase selector.

units.name: SelectTwoFrameObjectRecord
units.summary: Save the record base, increment field $0D and alternate the low selector bit from phase bit 3 before tail-calling record selection.

units.name: SelectFourPhaseObjectRecord
units.summary: Increment field $0D, use bits 3/4 to read the four-entry selector table and tail-call record selection.

units.name: SelectMaskedFourPhaseRecord
units.summary: Increment field $0D modulo 32, divide by eight and select one of four record bytes before record selection.

units.name: TestTrailingPartContacts
units.summary: Test auxiliary and player proximity against the trailing part. Ordinary misses return to the part updater; the supported contact path can discard one caller return frame before continuing the response. This requires the nested stack contract, not a universal ordinary-RTS summary.

units.name: PlayTransitionPulse
units.summary: Seed the direct pulse-2 transition tone and effect duration 1.

units.name: JoinAuxiliaryMotionUpdate
units.summary: Tail-call the existing main-bank auxiliary motion continuation.

units.name: JoinMainObjectRenderer
units.summary: Tail-call the fixed main-object render dispatch.

units.name: RestoreSavedObjectProgressA
units.summary: Restore coarse progress from the saved object value, clear projection coarse depth and run the palette/progression transition before its tone.

units.name: RestoreSavedObjectProgressB
units.summary: Restore the alternate saved coarse progress value and use the same transition and tone.

units.name: ClearFirstTwelveObjectTypes
units.summary: Clear type bytes in the first twelve sixteen-byte RAM records, then fall into the existing transition continuation.

units.name: RestoreCheckpointProgress
units.summary: Restore checkpoint coarse progress, clear its fine component and join the shared transition.

units.name: LoadTwoObjectPagesAndClearFront
units.summary: Advance the page selector twice through the object-grid loader, clear the first four RAM object types and reset the selector.

units.name: UpdateActionObjectRecord
units.summary: Load coordinates and variant from the active $63/$64 RAM record; advance its nonzero marked field only while unpaused. Project and return on rejection, otherwise tail-call vertical-object rendering and its conditional six-action contact dispatcher.

units.name: AdvanceWordWithCarryFold
units.summary: Save the original $3C/$3D word, shift it left, add the original word including shift carry, then fold the final carry into the low byte. The exact shift/add recurrence is established; its game-facing purpose remains unresolved.

units.name: StoreParserVariant
units.summary: Store X into field 6 through the parser RAM pointer $61/$62 and return. This domain is established by the parser caller, independently of the object walker $63/$64.

units.name: ReturnFromParserLowType
units.summary: Return from the supported low-type parser branch.

units.name: ReturnFromParserMarker
units.summary: Return from the supported marker parser branch.

units.name: PlayParsedObjectTone
units.summary: Queue sound $80 and initialize the direct pulse-2 parser effect. Return after setting its duration to $0F.

units.name: ReturnAfterClearingParsedType
units.summary: Return after the separate field-zero clear. It does not enter the ordinary record-initialization tail.

units.name: FinishOrdinaryParsedRecord
units.summary: Enter with Y=0 after the caller writes field 0. Write field 1 from $4D, field 4 from $4C, clear field 7 and toggle field $0C with XOR $FF. The prior value of field $0C is not assumed zero; all writes use the separately established parser RAM pointer.

units.name: UpdateControllerMirrorHelper
units.summary: Decrement the first OAM Y byte, write inverted frame-bit-zero to controller port bit 1, then save that value with bit 0 set in RAM $0F. This bounded helper does not choose a PRG bank.

units.name: SceneCoordinateSeed
units.summary: Fifteen coordinate/configuration bytes followed by the first byte of the next routine. The active initializer copies sixteen bytes starting here; that final copied source byte remains Code. This source boundary does not imply a sixteen-byte Data record.

units.name: SceneAlternatingEffectSelectors
units.summary: Three parallel two-byte arrays: X positions, Y positions and sprite record selectors. Frame bit 5 chooses one cell from each array.

units.name: SceneIntroPoseSequence
units.summary: Eight consecutive sprite selectors, one per eight-frame interval in the introductory pose sequence.

units.name: SceneWalkPoses
units.summary: Thirty-two walking sprite selectors indexed by (frame>>3)&31; values select records 7..9.

units.name: SceneSegmentPoses
units.summary: Eight rows of eight pose cells. The object selector chooses a row; the 32-step phase divided by four chooses a cell. Each cell is a local pose offset 0..4.

units.name: ScenePosePatternSuffix
units.summary: Sixteen repeated 0/1/2-valued bytes between the bounded pose grid and selector arrays. Neighboring consumers and patterns were inspected; a further pose row or original source schema is unresolved.

units.name: SceneSegmentRecordPairs
units.summary: Two parallel arrays of eight scene record selectors, indexed by the segment-animation selector.

units.name: SceneSegmentPaletteRecords
units.summary: Eight four-byte palette records. Each starts with a separator/padding byte followed by the three colors consumed for that segment selector. The palette consumer reads the last three cells.

units.name: SceneWaveCoordinateTriples
units.summary: Eight four-byte entries selected by (wave<<2)&31. The consumer reads signed coordinate/phase increments from the first three bytes; the fourth is zero backing. Values describe the scene wave mechanics; no original curve generator is asserted.

units.name: ScenePaletteRampSelectors
units.summary: Two four-step ramps. Frame divided by eight selects a step below four, then a saved 0-or-4 offset selects the ramp.

units.name: ScenePaletteSeparator
units.summary: One palette-valued byte between independently bounded ramp selectors and color records. Its original padding or record role is unresolved.

units.name: ScenePaletteRampColors
units.summary: Nine triples of palette colors on a four-byte stride. The final triple ends this 35-byte range; no unneeded fourth byte of the ninth record is included.

units.name: SceneInitialSpritePalette
units.summary: Sixteen sprite-palette bytes copied into scene RAM $80..$8F by the active graphics initializer.

units.name: SceneZeroGap
units.summary: Two zero bytes between a complete return and a separate helper. They have no established consumer or fill purpose.

units.name: SceneZeroTail
units.summary: Twenty-four zero bytes after a tail jump and before the unresolved truncated byte at $8600. Boundaries and neighboring control flow support generic noncode; fill purpose remains unknown.

units.name: LegacySceneInitialPalette
units.summary: Sixteen palette bytes copied by the duplicate initializer at $865A. They match the active palette; adjacent code is excluded.

units.name: SceneSpritePointers
units.summary: Forty-nine little-endian CPU pointers. The first record starts immediately after the prefix. Complete four-byte/FF records establish these bounds; this is not an inferred 128-selector domain. Targets can share suffixes.

units.name: LegacyMainLocalStopLoop
units.summary: Closed bank-local stop loop at CPU $8113 under banks [12,13,14,15]. Its only successor is itself, independent of registers or stack. No incoming accepted reference or natural reachability is established. The preceding $8110 call remains separately unknown.

units.name: LegacyBank10StackCallFragment
units.summary: Historical wrapper fragment at CPU $8076 under physical banks [10,11,14,15]. It clears scratch $0E, loads $FF for a stale external call, then encodes a save of stack-page byte $0101 around the local helper. The tail loads Y from $0E and A from X before RTS. External targets are current fixed-bank zero Data: no ordinary return, actual preservation, execution or natural entry is established. These are intended instruction mechanics, conditional on effects and returns that remain unresolved.

units.name: LegacyBank10RepeatedCallFragment
units.summary: Historical helper at CPU $808E. If its two initial calls return, compare scratch $06 with seven. A different value skips to the final call; seven is incremented before the three-call body. The body loads A=3, calls three stale targets, decrements $06 and repeats while nonzero. Callees may change scratch, flags, registers and stack, so eight iterations and eventual return are not established. Final call and RTS are retained instruction structure only; every external target remains Data.

units.name: LegacyBank10TransitionPrefix
units.summary: Historical main-transition prefix at CPU $81DC under physical banks [10,11,14,15]. It matches main-bank instructions at the same CPU origin, including the encoded main palette-tail call $8229. Here $8229 and fallthrough $8200 are zero Data. If that call returned, this prefix would clear $D0/$E3/$E1/$82, copy stage-record field $32 to $0712/$0732/$0752, then field $31 to $0711/$0731. It clips before the main counterpart stores $0751. No current routine, return, original build process, execution or natural reachability follows from the historical structure.
